# Scenario catalogue

*Generated by `scripts/generate_catalogue.py` from the cassettes. Do not edit by hand.*

One mock covers many test cases. Pick a scenario with the `X-Mock-Scenario` header:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_anything" \
     -H "X-Mock-Scenario: capacity-refusal" \
     -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/documents/upload
```

Over MCP, send the same header on the JSON-RPC request. If you cannot set headers at all
(`EventSource`, some MCP clients), set `SDMOCK_DEFAULT_SCENARIO` when starting the mock.

Two more headers are useful:

| Header | Effect |
|---|---|
| `X-Mock-Run: <id>` | An independent cursor, so two parallel runs of one scenario do not consume each other's job-state transitions. |
| `X-Mock-Latency: realistic` | Replay the recorded inter-event timings instead of firing instantly, to exercise a "still processing" UI against the real 30s-to-several-minute reality. |

`POST /__sdmock__/reset` rewinds every cursor. `GET /__sdmock__/catalogue` returns this
same information as JSON.

## How to read a scenario

**Recorded** scenarios were captured off `api.superdocs.app` against a synthetic corpus
authored for this repository. **Synthesised** ones were built from the documented shape
because they could not be observed responsibly — each says why, the mock sets
`X-Mock-Synthesised: true` on every response it serves from one, and the contract suite
skips them when it runs against the live service.


**12 scenarios — 9 recorded, 3 synthesised.** Default when no header is sent: `proposed-change-batch`.

### `account-status`

Account and quota calls: whoami (what an agent budgets from), the promotions balance it omits, and the documented 401 from the web-app-only usage endpoint.

*Recorded 2026-08-10 against `api.superdocs.app`.*

Interactions: 3. Behaviours exercised: B-005, B-092, B-093.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_anything" \
     -H "X-Mock-Scenario: account-status" \
     http://localhost:8080/v1/agents/whoami
```

### `capacity-refusal`

A document past the documented 25,000-sections-per-document scale limit, producing the structured 413 that carries limit_expandable: true, plus the documented recovery path.

*Recorded 2026-08-10 against `api.superdocs.app`.*

Interactions: 1. Behaviours exercised: B-070, B-073, B-074.

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_anything" \
     -H "X-Mock-Scenario: capacity-refusal" \
     http://localhost:8080/v1/documents/upload
```

### `large-file-upload`

The pre-signed upload flow: request a URL, PUT the bytes straight to storage, then parse by upload_id. Keeps large documents out of the request body, and returns the only response on the surface that declares ProcessDocumentResponse.

*Recorded 2026-08-10 against `api.superdocs.app`.*

Interactions: 2. Behaviours exercised: B-077, B-078, B-080, B-085, B-086, B-089, B-099.

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_anything" \
     -H "X-Mock-Scenario: large-file-upload" \
     http://localhost:8080/v1/uploads
```

### `large-multi-section-edit`

A whole-document edit across a 400-section register in compact response mode: sixteen operations in one turn, per-section chunk_diffs instead of full HTML, and the surgical-precision summary the service returns.  NOTE: this turn completed without pausing, so no continue_prompt was observed. The continue-prompt scenario is synthesised separately and labelled.

*Recorded 2026-08-10 against `api.superdocs.app`.*

Interactions: 3. Behaviours exercised: B-016, B-018, B-020, B-025, B-026, B-027, B-029, B-109, B-110.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_anything" \
     -H "X-Mock-Scenario: large-multi-section-edit" \
     http://localhost:8080/v1/jobs/my-job
```

### `paused-large-edit`

A very large edit that applies what it can, keeps that work, and pauses with awaiting_kind continue_prompt to ask whether to carry on -- plus the 409 that rejects /approve on a pause that needs /continue.

> **Synthesised, not recorded.** Reconstructed from /guides/async-jobs and /guides/streaming. A real 400-section whole-document edit was recorded first (16 operations) and completed without pausing, so the pause itself could not be observed inside the recording budget. The real large edit is recorded separately as large-multi-section-edit; this cassette carries only the pause.

Interactions: 3. Behaviours exercised: B-033, B-034, B-035, B-036, B-037, B-038, B-039, B-059.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_anything" \
     -H "X-Mock-Scenario: paused-large-edit" \
     http://localhost:8080/v1/jobs/my-job
```

### `rate-limit`

Quota exhaustion on a chat turn: the application 429, carrying Retry-After and the X-Usage-* headers that only appear on this response.

> **Synthesised, not recorded.** Reconstructed from /errors/rate-limits, which prints this response verbatim including its headers. Recording it live would mean spending the account's entire remaining operation balance to produce one fixture.

Interactions: 1. Behaviours exercised: B-019, B-064, B-065, B-067.

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_anything" \
     -H "X-Mock-Scenario: rate-limit" \
     http://localhost:8080/v1/chat
```

### `rate-limit-surge`

A platform-level throttle: a plain-text 429 with no Retry-After, which a client must treat as transient rather than as a quota problem.

> **Synthesised, not recorded.** Reconstructed from /errors/rate-limits. This response is emitted by the platform edge under load and cannot be induced by a single caller; attempting to would mean deliberately loading a live production service.

Interactions: 1. Behaviours exercised: B-066, B-067.

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_anything" \
     -H "X-Mock-Scenario: rate-limit-surge" \
     http://localhost:8080/v1/chat
```
